note: Private mutation/regression corpus for SwiftPropertyLaws — the law kit dogfooding on itself (Chapter 30 §30.4.4). Each mutant forces a law's property to always-true, so the law stops detecting its planted violator; the corresponding PlantedBugs detection test (which expects the violation) then fails. Run via `swift test --filter`. Not a scored benchmark.

mutants.label: Semigroup.combineAssociativity always returns true — a non-associative combine is no longer caught
Monoid.combineLeftIdentity always returns true — a broken left identity is no longer caught (detectsBadLeftIdentity asserts the specific law name)
Equatable.transitivity always returns true — a non-transitive == is no longer caught

Equatable.symmetry always returns true — an asymmetric == is no longer caught. Killable only after adding SymmetryOnlyEquatable (a `>=` violator that breaks symmetry alone) + detectsSymmetryOnlyEquality, which pins the symmetry law specifically.
Every.product sorts its bucket rectangles ignoring summed size, collapsing the ordering to row-major — the design decision the note measured as changing which failure gets reported.
Enumeration.prefix drops the original fullCount, so a truncated walk reports complete coverage of a space it only sampled the front of — the exact overclaim SpaceCoverage exists to prevent.
EnumerationDriver keeps walking past a failure, so the reported case is the last failure rather than the smallest — the minimality guarantee, silently lost.
Enumeration.map rebuilds the space as one size-0 bucket, so a mapped space loses its ordering contract and any product built on it degrades to row-major.
ViolationFormatter prints a replay seed for a walk, offering a handle that means nothing — a walk consumes no randomness and replays from its own space.
SpaceCoverage.isComplete requires strictly more cases than the space holds, so a complete walk never reports itself complete.

requiringApplicableCases treats every walk as if it were sampled, so a vacuous pass over a fully walked carrier still advises widening a generator that does not exist — the distinction between 'never sampled' and 'cannot exist' collapses back.

runTernaryLaw's enumerated arm walks pairs with a repeated third value instead of every triple, so a ternary law silently checks a diagonal slice of its input space while still reporting a complete walk.
EnumerationDriver reports only the address of a failing case, dropping the law's own explanation — the counterexample stays reproducible but stops saying what went wrong.
